title: Offline mode for the Marrowbook mobile app

sources.content: Proposal: let Marrowbook mobile users read and edit their recipe collections without a network connection. The app will keep a local copy of every recipe the user has opened in the last 30 days, stored in an encrypted on-device database. Edits made offline are queued and sent to the server when the connection returns. Photos are not cached in this phase because of storage limits on older phones; recipes show a placeholder image while offline.

Requirement: when an offline edit conflicts with a newer server version, the app must keep both versions and ask the user which to keep. Scenario: sync after reconnect. Given a user edited three recipes offline, when the device reconnects, then all three edits upload in the order they were made. Scenario: offline banner. Given the device has no connection, when the user opens the app, then a grey banner reading Offline appears at the top of the screen.

claims.text: Marrowbook keeps a local copy of every recipe opened in the last 30 days.
Marrowbook uploads offline edits in the order they were made.
When a Marrowbook offline edit conflicts with a newer server version, the app keeps both versions.
Marrowbook caches recipe photos for offline viewing.
The Marrowbook offline banner is grey.
Marrowbook offline mode will ship in the next app release.
